full_judgment:
13. Section 5 of the Limitation Act deals with the matter of condonation of delay; Sections 5 of the Limitation Act reads as follows: 

 "5. Extension of period of certain cases-Any appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this may be made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed thereof, when the appellant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period. 

 Explanation-The fact that the appellant or applicant was misled by any order, practice or judgment of the High Court Division in ascertaining or computing the prescribed period of limitation may be sufficient cause within the meaning of this section. 

 15. Although the Limitation Act does not provide for any specific period of limitation for invoking discretionary jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure but as per the long standing practice one has to file it without causing inordinate delay preferably within 90 days from the date of decree or order complained of as has been prescribed for preferring an appeal. 

 16. Although the Limitation Act does not provide for any specific period of limitation for invoking discretionary jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure but as long standing practice one has to file it without causing inordinate delay. In an appropriate case High Court Division may suo motu exercise such jurisdiction. 

 17. Section 5 of the Limitation Act has empowered to allow an application for a revision beyond the period of limitation if the petitioner can satisfy the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the revision application within the period of limitation. 

 22. It is the contention of the petitioners that they were not aware of the fate of the appeal; that perusing the papers left by the predecessor of the petitioners and thereafter communicating with their Advocate, they recently came to know about the fate of the Title Appeal No. 205 of 2003; that it took some time to get certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree and thereafter they communicated to the learned Advocate of this Court and handed over the papers; that it also took some time to draft the revisional application and to file the revision and thus there has been delay of 285 days in filing the revisional application. It is settled law that burden rests on the party who seeks indulgence of the Court in his favour to adduce distinct proof of, sufficient cause on which he relies. It is for the petitioner to show that his conduct throughout the period between the date of knowledge of the fate of appeal and filing of revision has been of such a character that it would be proper to condone the period of delay that has occurred beyond the period of limitation. 

 26. The extension of time under section 5 of the Limitation Act is a matter of concession which must be sanctioned under present circumstances. The legislature has conferred the power to condone delay by enacting section 5 of the Limitation Act in order to enable the Courts to do substantial justice by disposing of the matter on merit. 

 29. Having considered the entire materials on record, facts and circumstances referred above we are inclined to hold that the petitioners are legally and lawfully entitled to get indulgence under section 5 of the Limitation Act. Thus we find reasonable grounds to condone the delay.
